Theme

Body, health & movement

operation noun

surgical

also surgery, surgical operation, have an operation, operate on, surgery (the art)

classical

Plin. NH 25.150: ante sectiōnēs pūnctiōnēsque
M-O s.v. surgical operation
Traupman 169, 354

sectiō, sectiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an operation (literally, a cutting)

Lewis & Short: of the body only post-Augustan (Pliny; Celsus in Morgan–Owens); in Cicero sectiō is the auction of confiscated goods.

Other words

  • chīrurgia, chīrurgiae f. — surgery (the art)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cels. 7 praef. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 169, 388 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Cicero uses it figuratively of a violent remedy (Att. 4.3.3, Lewis & Short).

  • operātiō chīrurgica — a surgical operation

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. operation (surgical) (1846); Traupman 354: operātiō medica

    Classically operātiō is a working, labour or a religious service (Lewis & Short).

  • secō, secāre, secuī, sectum — operate on, cut

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 169 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • bibitur et contrā serpentēs et ante sectiōnēs pūnctiōnēsque, nē sentiantur

    it is drunk against snakebite, and before operations and lancings, so that they are not feltPlin. NH 25.150

  • manum adhibēre

    to use surgeryTraupman 388

See also operate, hospital, doctor, painkiller.
